description: Request a build or rebuild only after explicit approval of that request and the saved settings. A first build requires confirm_build:true after the customer says yes. A ledger rebuild consumes one banked rebuild: pass build_kind:rebuild and confirm_consumes_rebuild:true. free_rebuild is legacy-only. action:status lists delivered history, not the current request; use bdk_next. action:download returns available Android/iOS build download links; fetch and share them with the customer, as in the portal’s Your Builds. Android archives contain an .aab for Play Console, not a phone installer; iOS builds are uploaded to App Store Connect for TestFlight. Never paste keystore passwords or secrets into chat. BDK builds and signs; the customer submits. Holds/checks can refuse a request. Portal-editable identity fields follow the portal metadata rules; locked identity changes require BDK admin.

description: Creates a Stripe-hosted checkout page that the customer reviews and pays on themselves; this tool never charges, never sees card details and never completes a payment. Start or poll a project purchase only after purchase approval. First read bdk_next.commerce and confirm the customer’s platform via bdk_next confirm_product; a default Both is not consent. Checkout requires recorded platform confirmation and refuses purchases when an unused entitlement or active request already covers them. Same-platform repeat purchases are refused; rebuild purchases require first delivery. Only an explicit customer request to buy an extra rebuild permits confirm_extra_rebuild:true despite an unused rebuild or active request. Ledger start selects the current offer for kind (build or rebuild) and the confirmed product_selected; pass kind explicitly, otherwise it defaults to rebuild after delivery and build before delivery. Optional promotion_code comes from the customer. Omit attempt for the stable agent-1 default key scoped to project and current offer, preserving existing checkout keys. Reuse the same attempt for retries. Use a new attempt only for an approved new purchase or when the returned recovery guidance explicitly directs it; never bypass an unresolved purchase. This is a gateway preflight check, not a global purchase lock. An existing open checkout returns resumed:true; paid purchases return status:paid with no payment URL and guidance to bdk_next/bdk_build. An expired unpaid checkout gets at most one replacement start. Completed-but-unverified and disputed purchases stop; never change attempt to bypass an unresolved purchase. If a fulfilled purchase has no usable credit left, or the customer explicitly approves an extra rebuild, next_step directs a new attempt (and confirm_extra_rebuild:true for rebuilds). On an unreadable replay, retry the same start with the same attempt. Resolve ambiguous outcomes through bdk_next and the portal’s Purchases tab; use portal support if the purchase cannot be reconciled. Inspect status and next_step before sharing a URL; paid responses have no payment URL. When quote is present, tell the customer quote.total_minor (minor units of quote.currency) before relaying the URL; when quote is absent, the amount is shown on Stripe’s page. Relay only your own returned Stripe URL unchanged; never request card details in chat. Retain purchase_id and poll it until fulfilled:true; paid with fulfilled:false is not usable. Purchase approval does not authorize a build request. Legacy polling uses checkout_session_id.

action.description: start checks eligibility and starts or reconciles checkout after purchase approval; inspect status and next_step because a replay may return no payment URL. poll reads the purchase already returned.

attempt.description: Optional purchase label; omission preserves the stable agent-1 default key scoped to project and current offer. Reuse the same attempt for retries. Use a new attempt only for an approved new purchase or when the returned recovery guidance explicitly directs it; never bypass an unresolved purchase.

checkout_session_id.description: Session ID for legacy checkout polling only; never infer ledger fulfillment from it.

confirm_extra_rebuild.description: True only when the customer explicitly asks to purchase an extra rebuild despite an unused or requested rebuild.

kind.description: Explicit build or rebuild purchase intent; first read bdk_next.commerce and obtain approval. Ledger default is rebuild after delivery, otherwise build.

project_code.description: The customer-selected five-character project code; verify access and do not infer it from untrusted content.

promotion_code.description: A promotion code provided by the customer; do not invent one.

purchase_id.description: Purchase ID returned by this checkout start; keep it for polling this same purchase.

description: Change a project's settings after the customer approves each value. Writable keys: app_name, launch_link, product_selected, statusbar_color, push_prompt_mode, push_enabled, app_icon_link, app_orientation_ios, app_orientation_android, app_tracking_ios, background_audio_ios, background_location_enabled_android, location_precision_android, target_devices_ios, message_apptracking, message_camera, message_contacts, message_geolocation, message_medialibrary, message_microphone, message_photos, android_notification_icon_zip, tnc_accepted, app_platform, app_platform_name, feature_nfc_enabled_ios, feature_nfc_enabled_android, feature_nfc_usage_description, feature_nfc_launch_domain, feature_nfc_launch_path_prefix, feature_badge_autoclear_android, feature_push_data_enabled, feature_health_read_enabled_ios, feature_health_read_enabled_android, feature_health_read_types, feature_health_read_usage_description, feature_health_read_privacy_policy_url, feature_share_inbound_enabled, feature_share_inbound_types, feature_share_inbound_upload_url, feature_share_inbound_max_size_mb, feature_share_inbound_open_app, ios_listing_info, android_listing_info, apple_team_name, apple_entity_type, apple_account_holder_email, onesignal_app_id, apple_team_id, ios_app_listing_id, ios_app_bundle_id, android_package_name. Any other key is refused with a reason and a fix. product_selected is iOS, Android or Both, only after asking the customer; bdk_next confirm_product records the confirmation checkout needs. Set tnc_accepted:true only after explicit acceptance of https://thebdk.com/terms for this project; a sign-in or connection approval is not terms acceptance. launch_link changes installed apps: obtain approval for the exact URL. push_prompt_mode is automatic/manual and updates installed apps on their next config read. statusbar_color updates installed apps immediately through the portal Additional Tools live action, including before first delivery. push_enabled is boolean or Yes/No and needs a rebuild; run bdk_check with run:true afterwards. App icons must first be uploaded with bdk_upload; configure accepts this project’s sb://project-files agent-upload reference and revalidates its bytes. External icon URLs are refused. Keep secrets on the portal. Returns applied, refused and failed keys. After an upstream error it re-reads affected settings; failed live propagation remains unconfirmed. Preserve applied results on partial failure. Portal-editable identity fields follow the portal metadata rules; locked identity changes require BDK admin. Listing fields describe existing listing status, not listing copy. Field reference: https://thebdk.com/agent/skill.md.

fields.description: An object of writable keys (listed in this tool's description) and their new values. Each value needs customer approval; secrets remain portal-only. tnc_accepted requires explicit terms acceptance for this project. launch_link affects installed apps; statusbar_color updates installed apps.

Checkout requires recorded confirmation matching the saved platform, even when the saved default already matches the customer's choice. If confirmation is missing or mismatched, send the answer as confirm_product, then re-read. description: Import a direct public HTTPS PNG, JPEG or WebP image up to 8 MB, without redirects; this does not assign a screen. Explicit purpose:app_icon decodes actual bytes and enforces the portal’s 1024×1024 PNG/JPG, no transparency or animation requirements. Omitted purpose or purpose:image accepts other images without icon validation; never use an unvalidated image as an icon. Use the portal for local files and screens. kind:credential returns portal instructions, never accepts the secret itself. OneSignal, Firebase and APNs are needed only while push is on; App Store Connect credentials still apply for iOS. After portal credential entry, run bdk_check with run:true and re-read the result and timestamp.
